questions.q: Rohan's branch started from an old main. Main got a new commit since. What does git rebase main (run on Rohan's branch) do?
options: Copies Rohan's commits, one by one, on top of the newest main commit
Makes a merge commit with two parents
questions.explain: Rebase = give my commits a new base. Git sets them aside, moves the branch to main's newest commit, and replays them on top.

questions.q: After the rebase, Rohan's commit 79d769b is now 96286bf. Why did the hash change?
options: A hash includes the commit's parent; the parent changed, so these are new commits (copies)
questions.explain: Same message, author and change, but a different parent gives a different hash. Rebase always creates new commits.

questions.q: Rohan rebased free-delivery onto main. Then, on main, he runs git merge free-delivery. What happens?
options: A fast-forward: main was simply behind, so its label moves forward and the history is one straight line
A merge commit with two parents
questions.explain: After the rebase, free-delivery = main + 2 commits. main is just behind, so merging is a fast-forward.

questions.q: What is the golden rule of rebase?
options: Always rebase main onto your branch
Only rebase commits that nobody else has
questions.explain: Rebase replaces commits with new copies. If teammates already have the old ones, they end up with duplicates and a messy history.

questions.q: Merge vs rebase: what is the SAME after either one?
questions.explain: Both bring in the same changes, so the code ends up the same. Merge keeps a true record with a merge commit; rebase rewrites into a straight line.

questions.q: A rebase stops with a conflict. You fixed the file. What now?
options: git add the file, then git rebase --continue
questions.explain: git add marks it fixed; --continue replays the rest. (git rebase --abort cancels the whole rebase instead.)

questions.q: (Going deeper) After a rebase you want the old commits back. Which command finds them?
questions.explain: The reflog lists everywhere HEAD has been, including the old commits no branch points to any more. Then: git switch -c rescue <old-hash>.

questions.q: (Going deeper) In git rebase -i, what does changing pick to squash do?
options: Joins that commit into the one above it
questions.explain: squash combines commits (keeping both messages for you to edit). fixup does the same but drops the message; drop removes a commit.
